packageRules.description: Renovate does not write mise locks. Its lock update ran the runner's own mise, which disagreed with the repository's base on platforms and graphs, and moving a pin without its lock left the dev image unbuildable (standards#1084). The post-upgrade `just generate` relocks `image/mise.lock` for the fleet's three platforms in the base the repository's Dockerfile names, then runs the repository's other generation (standards#1086, Decisions 5 and 6).

mise `github:` tools pinned bare (`"2.20.0"`) follow tags such as `v2.20.2`. Renovate's mise github backend adds an extractVersion only for a `version_prefix` option (its aqua and ubi backends strip the `v`), so a bump wrote `v2.20.2` into image/mise.toml while mise locks `version = "2.20.2"`, and the locked-tools Check rejected it. Strip the prefix to keep the pin bare.
Biome is owned only by the standards mise floor. Freeze npm manifest copies (including upstream fork pins) without disabling custom.regex floor/schema bumps in standards.
Ruff is owned only by the standards mise floor. Freeze PyPI manifest copies, including optional/dev groups and requirements, while leaving standards custom.regex pipx floor bumps enabled.

Do not automatically raise the consumer-owned pyproject.toml requires-python compatibility FLOOR on every CPython patch. Renovate bumped >=3.14.6 to >=3.14.7 while the pinned Python and uv 0.12.1 still provided at most 3.14.6, making uv lock and CI fail. Raise the floor deliberately alongside the repository's Python pin in image/mise.toml; ordinary pep621 package updates stay enabled.

Do not automatically raise a package's published package.json engines.node compatibility FLOOR on every Node patch; same principle as the requires-python rule above. Renovate bumped pi-agent-browser-native from >=24.21.0 to >=24.22.3, which silently narrows the consumers it supports and broke the test that ties the floor to the code's runtime floor and its documented, qualified support contract. Raise the floor deliberately, with that code and qualification. The repository's Node pin in image/mise.toml, @types/node, devEngines and other engines keep updating.

Disable Terraform CORE version bumps (`required_version` in versions.tf) across onboarded consumers. Renovate raises the constraint in git, but the executing version lives OUTSIDE git — it is the HCP Terraform workspace's own `terraform-version` setting — and nothing raises that. A merged bump therefore makes every run in that workspace fail at `terraform init` with `Error: Unsupported Terraform Core version`, which stays invisible until someone needs an apply. Measured: agent-workspaces#113 raised the constraint to >= 1.15.9, the workspace stayed on 1.15.8, and every run errored for two weeks — found only when an outage fix could not be applied. Raising Terraform core is a paired, deliberate move (raise the workspace setting, then merge the constraint), so it is not background maintenance. NOTE: scoped to the core-version depType only; provider and module updates under the terraform manager are unaffected.

Pin only named Python dev tools in pep621 dev groups: rangeStrategy:bump writes pyright>=1.1.413, then uv lock resolves 1.1.414 while it is inside the seven-day soak, and Renovate's artifact guard rejects the lockfile. An exact pin keeps the selected, aged version and its uv resolution aligned; runtime and optional dependencies retain their own range strategy.

A `pin` update writes the exact version the current range already allows, usually the one the lock already resolves, so it adopts no new release and the seven-day soak has nothing to age. Renovate wires no release timestamp into `pin` updates (renovatebot/renovate#40288), so under timestamp-required every pin branch otherwise holds renovate/stability-days pending forever; Renovate's own security:minimumReleaseAge presets opt `pin` out for the same reason. Pins still merge only when green. `pinDigest` and every version update keep the soak.

Hold TypeScript 7 only where the current version is below 7: TypeScript 7 removes baseUrl and moduleResolution=node10, and typescript-eslint and @astrojs/check peer ranges do not yet support it. Lift the hold when both support TypeScript 7; repositories already on 7 continue receiving 7.x.

Standing automerge for the safe classes: non-major updates (minor/patch/pin/digest/pinDigest) of stable >=1.0.0 deps, every manager, dev and runtime alike. Subsumes the previous devDependencies and github-actions/dockerfile rules. Majors stay manual; the next rule arms the same non-major updates for pre-1.0 dependencies. The require-review fallback sets platformAutomerge:false so Renovate's own engine performs the merge as the bypassed Renovate App. GitHub-native auto-merge waits only on required checks, while Renovate's own engine waits for every check, so the original onboarded set had too few required contexts for a safe native handoff. The 2026-07-30 gate-tests rollout added the repo-owned required `test-gate` context for the 34 repos carrying `gate_tests=true`; `.github-private`#179 then closed the same-day lint/e2e gap by making `lint-hooks / lint-hooks` and `e2e / e2e` required through property-targeted org rulesets. The seven governed repos without test-gate carry zero language facets except playwright-skills, so their lack of a test context is not an unfixed rollout hole. Renovate's own engine is stricter here because it waits for every check the consumer actually renders, not only the checks required before GitHub merges.

Pre-1.0 minor, patch, pin, digest and pinDigest updates inherit the same Renovate-side automerge and release-age policy as stable dependencies. Semver allows breaking changes in a 0.x minor, so green checks are the guard. Keep this rule before the language feature and image holds. Renovate-classified majors still become drafts.

Hold Python minor updates to mise, asdf and .python-version pins. Python 3.x to 3.y is a language feature version: removed APIs and missing wheels can break consumers, so treat it like a major. Patch updates keep the standing automerge.
Hold Go language feature versions (1.x to 1.y) in go.mod go and toolchain directives. Treat them like majors; patch raises inherit the standing automerge.

Lockfile maintenance only refreshes transitive resolution inside existing ranges - the lowest-risk update class. minimumReleaseAge:0 is required for the automerge to ever fire: under the global 7-day soak, Renovate stamps its own `renovate/stability-days` pending status whenever any refreshed transitive release is younger than 7 days, its merge engine waits for ALL checks including that one, and the next weekly refresh pulls new young releases that re-arm the clock - so the PR stays green-but-unmergeable indefinitely (standards#404 sat 8 days; hand-merged 2026-08-03). The soak exists to vet just-published DIRECT updates; lockfile refreshes stay inside ranges already vetted by their own PRs.

Ungrouped stable npm minor and patch updates share one rolling PR while inheriting the standing safe automerge posture. The current-version guard keeps pre-1.0 packages out, and the JSONata guard preserves an earlier narrower monorepo group.

Ungrouped pre-1.0 npm minor and patch updates share one rolling PR in a branch distinct from stable npm updates, so a pre-1.0 update that fails its checks cannot stall the stable branch. They inherit the pre-1.0 automerge rule above. The JSONata guard preserves an earlier narrower monorepo group.

Ungrouped stable Cargo minor and patch updates share one rolling PR while inheriting the standing safe automerge posture. The current-version guard keeps pre-1.0 crates out, and the JSONata guard preserves an earlier narrower monorepo group.

Ungrouped pre-1.0 Cargo minor and patch updates share one rolling PR in a branch distinct from stable Cargo updates, so a pre-1.0 update that fails its checks cannot stall the stable branch. They inherit the pre-1.0 automerge rule above. The JSONata guard preserves an earlier narrower monorepo group.

Ungrouped stable dependency pin updates share a safe automerge branch without being blocked by a pre-1.0 pin. The JSONata guard preserves earlier narrower groups, and later package-specific grouping rules remain authoritative.

Keep ungrouped pre-1.0 dependency pins on a branch distinct from stable pins. They inherit the pre-1.0 automerge rule. The JSONata guard preserves earlier narrower groups, and later package-specific grouping rules remain authoritative.
Keep the Python input separate from action updates so its minor-version hold does not hold the action group.
Hold Python minor updates in workflow inputs. Python 3.x to 3.y is a language feature version: removed APIs and missing wheels can break consumers, so treat it like a major.

The starter standards.yml is copied from the standards package and reported as Starter Drift when it differs. Its action pins advance in the package's starter, so per-consumer github-actions updates in this file are disabled to keep it identical. First-party .github calls follow main and are disabled separately for every caller.

First-party fast lane for org-published OCI artifacts. The global 7-day minimumReleaseAge is a supply-chain soak for just-published THIRD-PARTY versions; an artifact the org itself publishes to ghcr.io/rubio-enterprises (Dev Container features, container images) was already gated by review and CI on the PR that released it, so there is nothing to vet. null, not "0 days": a Dev Container feature's OCI manifest carries no creation timestamp, and Renovate's default minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour (timestamp-required) never treats an untimestamped release as stable, so any age requirement at all would hold these updates forever. Scoped to the docker datasource and the ghcr.io/rubio-enterprises/ prefix because GHCR enforces org ownership of that namespace; the bare `rubio-enterprises/` docker name is deliberately NOT matched — it resolves to Docker Hub, whose namespaces are first-come and not provably the org's. The age exemption does not widen automerge. Majors remain held drafts; pre-1.0 minor and patch updates automerge through the pre-1.0 rule above, here with no soak.

First-party fast lane for org-owned GitHub sources: reusable workflows and actions, GitHub releases/tags/digests, git tags/refs and Go modules under github.com/Rubio-Enterprises. Same rationale as the GHCR rule above: these releases are cut by the org's own reviewed merges, so the third-party soak protects nothing. Matched only on datasources whose package name is a GitHub owner path, because GitHub enforces that the Rubio-Enterprises owner is the org; never on publisher-declared metadata such as sourceUrl (any third-party npm/PyPI package can claim a github.com/Rubio-Enterprises repository URL) or on bare package names in public registries (dependency confusion). The trailing slash anchors the owner exactly, so look-alike owners such as Rubio-Enterprises-x do not match. The age exemption does not widen automerge. Majors remain held drafts; pre-1.0 minor and patch updates automerge through the pre-1.0 rule above, here with no soak.

First-party .github workflows and actions follow main directly. Do not pin or update this dependency in any caller, including repository-owned TestFlight release workflows; third-party action updates retain their existing policy.

Runtime dependency updates that change a shipped tool (`rubio-cli-kit` or `typer`) must use `fix(deps)` so release-please cuts a patch release. This rule changes commit semantics only; the standing automerge and hold rules are unchanged.

Group related tool runtime dependencies even when Typer is 0.x. A kit release can raise its Typer floor; separate branches make uv lock fail before either PR exists. This rule controls grouping only. Automerge remains per-upgrade, and Renovate automerges a branch only when every upgrade is automerge-enabled. Pre-1.0 Typer non-major updates inherit the standing automerge and release-age policy. Neither rule here changes release age. Typer is a third-party PyPI package and keeps the global 7-day soak: every uv project sets exclude-newer = "7 days", so uv cannot lock a younger Typer and a zero-age Typer update fails its relock. rubio-cli-kit keeps its zero-age fast lane through the first-party GitHub sources rule above, because consumers take it as a uv git source on github.com/Rubio-Enterprises, which exclude-newer does not filter.

Stable non-major tool runtime dependencies automerge: Renovate merges as soon as every check passes. Grouping is separate above so a coupled 0.x Typer floor update remains solvable. Majors remain manual; 0.x non-major updates automerge through the pre-1.0 rule above instead of this one. Release age follows the group rule above: Typer waits the global soak, rubio-cli-kit does not.

Git-sourced uv-tools entries must resolve readable tags to immutable commit SHAs. This narrow rule owns pinDigests because it is a package option, not a custom-manager field; keeping it independent of update type and current version lets Renovate bootstrap a tag-only entry before it can classify the resulting pinDigest update.

Git-sourced tool pins in `home/.chezmoidata/uv-tools.toml` are authoritative first-party inputs for the org. Group stable non-major tag/SHA advances into one PR, skip the org release-age soak, and use Renovate-side automerge. Major tool releases stay manual. A 0.x tool's non-major updates inherit the pre-1.0 rule above, in their own PR outside this group.
Group mise CLI updates, including the marked MISE_VERSION fallback when present. Non-major updates inherit the standing automerge policy.
Group uv CLI updates tracked by the workflow version marker when present. Non-major updates inherit the standing automerge policy.
Keep the Standards base and runner images floating on :main outside Dockerfiles. Versioned Release Pins keep the normal update policy.
Pin and refresh the Standards base and runner :main digests together in Dockerfiles, with Renovate-side automerge.
Per-repository prebuilt Dev Container images deliberately float on :main. They are private packages unavailable to Renovate; do not look up versions or pin digests in any Docker-datasource manager.
Update npm packages in the earendil-works family together, including major updates.
Update the Dockerfile Python pin with the repository mise Python pin.
Hold Python minor updates to Dockerfile version pins. Python 3.x to 3.y is a language feature version: removed APIs and missing wheels can break consumers, so treat it like a major.

Group Docker Hub `python` base image updates with the repository's mise Python pin and ENV UV_PYTHON. The next rule holds language feature versions for review. Grouping does not freeze the branch: a member still inside its seven-day age is left out, and the others go ahead.
Hold Python minor updates to Docker Hub Python images. Python 3.x to 3.y is a language feature version: removed APIs and missing wheels can break consumers, so treat it like a major.

Images on any registry other than Docker Hub arrive without the seven-day age, and a person merges them (owner's decision of 2026-11-20 on .github-private#722). Renovate's docker datasource dates a tag only on Docker Hub, from the `tag_last_pushed` field of the Docker Hub API. ghcr.io, lscr.io, quay.io, mcr.microsoft.com and every other registry give no release date, so under the default timestamp-required every tag, digest and pinDigest update of such an image was held for ever, with no pull request and no signal. timestamp-optional lets an undated update through; an update that does carry a date still waits its seven days. automerge is off because nothing has aged these updates. The selector follows Renovate's own registry detection (a first path segment that contains a dot or a colon names a registry), so a new registry needs no edit here. Docker Hub names, bare or spelled docker.io, index.docker.io or registry-1.docker.io, do not match and keep their dates, soak and automerge. The first-party ghcr.io/rubio-enterprises images do not match and keep their fast lane and automerge. Keep this rule after the standing and pre-1.0 automerge rules, which it disarms, and before the held rule, which still makes majors held drafts.

Docker Hub digest and pinDigest updates arrive without a release date: Renovate's docker datasource dates Docker Hub tags from `tag_last_pushed` but gives a rebuilt digest none, so under timestamp-required they stayed pending on `renovate/stability-days` for ever (mac-dev-playbook's postgres, redis and sockpuppetbrowser digests, 2026-11). timestamp-optional lets an undated digest through and a person merges it, as for other registries (.github-private#722); a dated update still waits its seven days. The next rule re-arms automerge for official images only. Tag updates keep their dates, soak and automerge. The selector is the complement of the rule above: a name whose first segment has no dot or colon, or that starts with a Docker Hub host. Same position constraints as the rule above.

Docker Official Images (`docker.io/library/*`, also written bare, as `library/...` or with another Docker Hub host) automerge their undated digest and pinDigest updates (owner's decision of 2026-11-21). Docker builds them from reviewed changes in the public docker-library repositories, so a bad rebuild needs a compromise of Docker's own pipeline, where a third-party image needs only its publisher's token. Third-party Docker Hub images and other registries still need a person. Keep this rule directly after the Docker Hub digest rule and before the held rule.

Renovate-classified majors are held drafts, including 0.x updates classified as major. Concurrent limits share the repository backlog count: a held draft opens only when no other Renovate PR is open, and one unattended draft cannot fill all five slots. Closing it declines that version. Keep this rule last so earlier rules cannot re-arm a major.

customManagers.description: Track the Dockerfile interpreter pin using the same source as the mise Python tool.
uv CLI pin on astral-sh/setup-uv's `version:` input. Mirrors the jdx/mise manager above; no extractVersionTemplate because astral-sh/uv tags are bare semver (`0.12.1`), not v-prefixed like mise's.

Git-sourced uv-tools entries use recursive matching: the outer expression binds one TOML table to its GitHub repo, and the inner expression replaces only that table's `version` line. The paired package rule enables `pinDigests` so tag-only entries bootstrap, and the explicit replacement always writes the immutable SHA plus readable tag (`version = "<sha>"  # vX.Y.Z`).
